blocks.en: Chapala Theological Seminary, a ministry of Common Ground Fellowship | Professor: Dr. Wayne Cook | Director: Dr. Ted Rogers

blocks.en: This course is drawn from the worship curriculum of Dr. Wayne Cook, who served eleven years as Professor of Pastoral Ministries and Preaching, together with the teaching of Andi Cook, who taught alongside him at the seminary. It reflects not only academic study but decades of pastoral and seminary experience.
blocks.es_reference: Este curso proviene del currículo de adoración del Dr. Wayne Cook, quien sirvió once años como Profesor de Ministerios Pastorales y Predicación, junto con la enseñanza de Andi Cook, quien enseñó a su lado en el seminario. Refleja no solo el estudio académico sino décadas de experiencia pastoral y de seminario.

blocks.en: I. The Medieval Darkening
blocks.es_reference: I. El oscurecimiento medieval

blocks.en: By the Middle Ages, worship had drifted far from the simple service Justin Martyr described. The clergy and the people became detached from one another. The priest stood at the altar with his back to the people, performing the mass in Latin, a language the ordinary worshipper could no longer understand. The Scriptures remained in the hands of the priests, since few could read. This was, in a real sense, a return to Babel, the very opposite of Pentecost, where every man heard the gospel in his own tongue. Several theological developments deepened the darkness: Mariolatry made Mary an intercessor; confession became a system of prescribed forgiveness; indulgences were sold by men like Tetzel, whose crude slogan promised that when the coin in the coffer clinks, the soul from Purgatory springs; and transubstantiation taught that the bread and wine literally became the body and blood of Christ.
blocks.es_reference: Para la Edad Media, la adoración se había alejado mucho del sencillo servicio que Justino Mártir describió. El clero y el pueblo se separaron unos de otros. El sacerdote estaba en el altar con la espalda al pueblo, realizando la misa en latín, un idioma que el adorador común ya no podía entender. Las Escrituras permanecían en manos de los sacerdotes, ya que pocos sabían leer. Esto fue, en un sentido real, un regreso a Babel, lo opuesto mismo de Pentecostés, donde cada hombre oyó el evangelio en su propia lengua. Varios desarrollos teológicos profundizaron la oscuridad: la mariolatría hizo de María una intercesora; la confesión se volvió un sistema de perdón prescrito; las indulgencias eran vendidas por hombres como Tetzel, cuyo lema vulgar prometía que cuando la moneda en el cofre suena, el alma del Purgatorio brinca; y la transubstanciación enseñaba que el pan y el vino literalmente se volvían el cuerpo y la sangre de Cristo.

blocks.en: II. The Reformation and Its Reformers
blocks.es_reference: II. La Reforma y sus reformadores

blocks.en: Then God raised up the Reformation, and the Reformers tried to return worship to its New Testament pattern. They conducted services in the language of the people. They moved the altar into the view of the congregation. They put the Scriptures back into the hands of the members, and they rediscovered preaching, so that the sixteenth century became one of the great centuries of preaching. Above all they recovered the priesthood of all believers, which Luther so strongly stressed.
blocks.es_reference: Entonces Dios levantó la Reforma, y los reformadores intentaron regresar la adoración a su patrón del Nuevo Testamento. Conducían los servicios en el idioma del pueblo. Movieron el altar a la vista de la congregación. Pusieron las Escrituras de vuelta en manos de los miembros, y redescubrieron la predicación, de modo que el siglo dieciséis se volvió uno de los grandes siglos de la predicación. Sobre todo recuperaron el sacerdocio de todos los creyentes, que Lutero tan fuertemente enfatizó.

blocks.en: The reformers of worship differed among themselves. Martin Luther meant only to reform Rome, not to break with it, and he taught consubstantiation against transubstantiation. Ulrich Zwingli was the radical, treating the Lord's Supper as pure symbol and even abolishing music from his services. John Calvin instituted congregational singing, emphasized the Lord's Supper, and produced the Genevan Service Book that shaped Reformed worship across France, Switzerland, Holland, and Scotland.
blocks.es_reference: Los reformadores de la adoración diferían entre sí. Martín Lutero solo quería reformar a Roma, no romper con ella, y enseñó la consubstanciación contra la transubstanciación. Ulrico Zwinglio fue el radical, tratando la Cena del Señor como puro símbolo y hasta aboliendo la música de sus servicios. Juan Calvino instituyó el canto congregacional, enfatizó la Cena del Señor, y produjo el Libro de Servicio de Ginebra que moldeó la adoración reformada por toda Francia, Suiza, Holanda, y Escocia.

blocks.en: Calvin deserves a special word, because he gave the Reformed tradition its enduring emphasis on the mind. Calvin was famous for organizing his teaching into points, subpoints, and sub-subpoints. The strength of this is that it appeals to the mind and takes the truth-half of John 4:24 with full seriousness. The weakness, when carried too far, is that it can become dry, points and subpoints that feed the head but may not reach the heart. And this brings us back to spirit and truth. Worship in spirit and in truth is the both-and. We humans are not one-dimensional. We give God our minds AND our praise, the carefully reasoned sermon AND the heart lifted up in song.
blocks.es_reference: Calvino merece una palabra especial, porque dio a la tradición reformada su énfasis perdurable en la mente. Calvino fue famoso por organizar su enseñanza en puntos, subpuntos, y sub-subpuntos. La fortaleza de esto es que apela a la mente y toma la mitad de la verdad de Juan 4:24 con plena seriedad. La debilidad, cuando se lleva muy lejos, es que puede volverse seco, puntos y subpuntos que alimentan la cabeza pero pueden no alcanzar el corazón. Y esto nos trae de vuelta al espíritu y la verdad. Adorar en espíritu y en verdad es el ambos-y. Los seres humanos no somos unidimensionales. Damos a Dios nuestra mente Y nuestra alabanza, el sermón cuidadosamente razonado Y el corazón levantado en canto.

blocks.en: III. The Two Great Schisms
blocks.es_reference: III. Los dos grandes cismas

blocks.en: The Western church we have been describing is only half of Christendom, and most Protestants confuse two very different splits. The first split came in AD 451 at the Council of Chalcedon. Six ancient churches refused the council's formula that Christ is one Person in two natures, holding instead to miaphysitism, the doctrine that Christ is fully divine and fully human in one nature. These are the Oriental Orthodox churches: the Coptic of Egypt, the Ethiopian and Eritrean, the Syriac, the Armenian, and the Malankara of India. They have existed in unbroken continuity for more than fifteen centuries.
blocks.es_reference: La iglesia occidental que hemos estado describiendo es solo la mitad de la cristiandad, y la mayoría de los protestantes confunden dos divisiones muy diferentes. La primera división vino en el año 451 en el Concilio de Calcedonia. Seis iglesias antiguas rechazaron la fórmula del concilio de que Cristo es una Persona en dos naturalezas, sosteniendo en cambio el miafisismo, la doctrina de que Cristo es plenamente divino y plenamente humano en una naturaleza. Estas son las iglesias ortodoxas orientales: la copta de Egipto, la etíope y la eritrea, la siríaca, la armenia, y la malankara de India. Han existido en continuidad ininterrumpida por más de quince siglos.

blocks.en: The second split came in AD 1054, the Great Schism, when the Patriarch of Constantinople and the Pope of Rome excommunicated one another. The east became the Eastern Orthodox Church; the west became the Roman Catholic Church. Those mutual excommunications stood for more than nine hundred years and were not lifted until 1965. There is also a third stream, the Eastern Catholic or Uniate churches, which kept the Eastern liturgical forms but returned to communion with Rome. To know worship, the Protestant student must know that the church is far wider and far older than his own tradition.
blocks.es_reference: La segunda división vino en el año 1054, el Gran Cisma, cuando el Patriarca de Constantinopla y el Papa de Roma se excomulgaron uno al otro. El oriente se volvió la Iglesia Ortodoxa Oriental; el occidente se volvió la Iglesia Católica Romana. Esas excomuniones mutuas se mantuvieron por más de novecientos años y no fueron levantadas hasta 1965. Hay también una tercera corriente, las iglesias católicas orientales o uniatas, que mantuvieron las formas litúrgicas orientales pero regresaron a la comunión con Roma. Para conocer la adoración, el estudiante protestante debe saber que la iglesia es mucho más amplia y mucho más antigua que su propia tradición.

blocks.en: IV. Furniture, the Frontier, and the Black Church
blocks.es_reference: IV. El mobiliario, la frontera, y la iglesia negra

blocks.en: One of the most visible changes of the Reformation was furniture, and the rearrangement was theology. The medieval Catholic sanctuary placed the altar at the center, the priest facing it, the sacrament supreme. The Reformers moved the pulpit to the center. This was not decoration; it was a confession. The medieval room said salvation comes through the sacrament; the Reformed room said salvation comes through the preached Word. We will return to this in Unit 10, for the room itself preaches.
blocks.es_reference: Uno de los cambios más visibles de la Reforma fue el mobiliario, y la reorganización era teología. El santuario católico medieval colocaba el altar en el centro, el sacerdote mirándolo, el sacramento supremo. Los reformadores movieron el púlpito al centro. Esto no era decoración; era una confesión. La sala medieval decía que la salvación viene por el sacramento; la sala reformada decía que la salvación viene por la Palabra predicada. Volveremos a esto en la Unidad 10, porque la sala misma predica.

blocks.en: Worship kept developing. In the nineteenth century, three forces shaped it: revivalism, which gave Baptists the invitation; romanticism, born at Oxford, which revived Gothic architecture; and denominationalism, which split many bodies over racial and other issues. And out of that painful history came one of the most important streams of all, the African American church. Forged first in the secret praise meetings of slaves, where worship was sometimes forbidden, it grew into a powerful tradition drawing on the spirituals, on call-and-response forms older than slavery, and on a theology of suffering and deliverance read straight out of Exodus and the Psalms. It became its own tradition, and we will say more of its worship in Unit 10.
blocks.es_reference: La adoración siguió desarrollándose. En el siglo diecinueve, tres fuerzas la moldearon: el avivamiento, que dio a los bautistas la invitación; el romanticismo, nacido en Oxford, que revivió la arquitectura gótica; y el denominacionalismo, que dividió a muchos cuerpos por asuntos raciales y otros. Y de esa dolorosa historia vino una de las corrientes más importantes de todas, la iglesia afroamericana. Forjada primero en las reuniones secretas de alabanza de los esclavos, donde la adoración a veces era prohibida, creció hasta volverse una tradición poderosa que toma de los espirituales, de formas de llamado y respuesta más antiguas que la esclavitud, y de una teología de sufrimiento y liberación leída directamente del Éxodo y los Salmos. Se volvió su propia tradición, y diremos más de su adoración en la Unidad 10.

sa.prompt: Describe how clergy and people became detached in medieval worship, and why Latin worship was a return to Babel.
sa.model: In medieval worship, the priest stood at the altar with his back to the people, performing the mass in Latin, a language ordinary worshippers could no longer understand, while the Scriptures remained locked in the hands of priests since few could read. This detachment made Latin worship a return to Babel because it was the very opposite of Pentecost, where every man heard the gospel in his own tongue — instead of understanding drawing people together, incomprehensible language kept clergy and people apart.

sa.prompt: Explain the four theological developments of medieval worship: Mariolatry, confession, indulgences, and transubstantiation.
sa.model: Mariolatry made Mary an intercessor, adding a mediator beyond Christ alone. Confession became a system of prescribed forgiveness administered by priests rather than direct access to God. Indulgences were sold by men like Tetzel, whose crude slogan promised that when the coin in the coffer clinks, the soul from Purgatory springs, turning grace into a commercial transaction. Transubstantiation taught that the bread and wine literally became the body and blood of Christ, elevating the ritual itself to a place Scripture never gave it.

sa.prompt: How did the Reformation try to return worship to the New Testament pattern?
sa.model: The Reformation tried to return worship to the New Testament pattern by conducting services in the language of the people, moving the altar into the view of the congregation, putting the Scriptures back into the hands of the members, and rediscovering preaching. Above all, the Reformers recovered the priesthood of all believers, which Luther so strongly stressed, removing the barrier between clergy and people that medieval worship had built up.

sa.prompt: Compare the worship contributions of Luther, Zwingli, and Calvin.
sa.model: Luther meant only to reform Rome, not break with it, and taught consubstantiation against transubstantiation. Zwingli was the radical, treating the Lord's Supper as pure symbol and even abolishing music from his services. Calvin instituted congregational singing, emphasized the Lord's Supper, and produced the Genevan Service Book that shaped Reformed worship across France, Switzerland, Holland, and Scotland — each Reformer left a distinct and lasting mark on worship practice.

sa.prompt: Calvin emphasized points and subpoints, appealing to the mind. Discuss the strength and weakness of this, and how John 4:24 corrects it.
sa.model: Calvin's emphasis on points, subpoints, and sub-subpoints appeals to the mind, taking the truth-half of John 4:24 with full seriousness — its strength is careful, sound doctrine. Its weakness, when carried too far, is that it can become dry, feeding the head but not reaching the heart. John 4:24's call to worship in spirit and in truth corrects this by insisting on the both-and: we give God our minds and our praise, the carefully reasoned sermon and the heart lifted up in song.

sa.prompt: Explain the first great split of AD 451 at Chalcedon and the Oriental Orthodox churches.
sa.model: The first great split came at the Council of Chalcedon in AD 451, when six ancient churches refused the council's formula that Christ is one Person in two natures, holding instead to miaphysitism — the doctrine that Christ is fully divine and fully human in one nature. These became the Oriental Orthodox churches: the Coptic of Egypt, the Ethiopian and Eritrean, the Syriac, the Armenian, and the Malankara of India, existing in unbroken continuity for over fifteen centuries.

sa.prompt: Explain the Great Schism of 1054 between East and West.
sa.model: The Great Schism of 1054 occurred when the Patriarch of Constantinople and the Pope of Rome excommunicated one another, splitting the church into the Eastern Orthodox Church in the east and the Roman Catholic Church in the west. Those mutual excommunications stood for more than nine hundred years and were not lifted until 1965, showing how deep and lasting the division became.

sa.prompt: Explain the three forces that shaped nineteenth-century worship: revivalism, romanticism, and denominationalism.
sa.model: Revivalism gave rise to the evangelistic invitation still used in many churches. Romanticism, born at Oxford, revived Gothic architecture, shaping how many church buildings looked and felt. Denominationalism split many church bodies over racial and other issues, fragmenting Christendom along new lines in the nineteenth century, each of these three forces leaving a lasting mark on how churches gathered and worshipped.

sa.prompt: Explain how the Reformation rearrangement of furniture (moving the pulpit to the center) was a theological statement.
sa.model: The medieval Catholic sanctuary placed the altar at the center with the priest facing it, making the sacrament supreme; the Reformers moved the pulpit to the center instead. This was not mere decoration but a confession in physical form: the medieval room said salvation comes through the sacrament, while the Reformed room said salvation comes through the preached Word — the very architecture of the room preached a theology.

sa.prompt: Describe the African American church as a major post-Reformation worship tradition.
sa.model: The African American church was forged first in the secret praise meetings of slaves, where worship was sometimes forbidden, and grew into a powerful tradition drawing on the spirituals, on call-and-response forms older than slavery, and on a theology of suffering and deliverance read straight out of Exodus and the Psalms. It became its own major worship tradition, born out of painful history but rich in resilient faith.
